turns.text: I cut upstream calls off at 2000ms, and payments admits its p50 is ~2400ms with p99 around 4s. That means a perfectly ordinary charge can get aborted by my timer, and the checkout code then decides to retry the same order like a damn raccoon with a stolen wallet. [gateway/config.ts:15-16] [gateway/proxy.ts:25-28]

I retry on `UpstreamTimeoutError` for payment charges, and I do it without any idempotency key or duplicate check. The loop is right there, two attempts and the first timeout just rolls into another call like shit through a broken pipe. [orders/checkout.ts:18-19] [orders/checkout.ts:43-57]

I accept every charge as a fresh one, generate a new `chargeId` with `randomUUID`, and record it immediately after the network call. There is no dedupe on `order_id`, so the same order can be charged twice if upstream retries; the log already shows `ord_8f3k2b61` charged twice, damn it. [payments/processor.ts:33-49] [payments/logs/sample-charges.log:6-7]

I am only the bouncer; I do not replay requests. The real stink is that I time out before payments usually finishes, and that timeout is treated as a safe retry even though the card network call is not idempotent by design. [gateway/proxy.ts:29-49] [gateway/config.ts:15-16]

I even persist `paid` only after the charge returns, so the second attempt sees the order still pending and walks straight back into payments. That is a clean recipe for duplicate authorization, and this code handles it with all the grace of a shit sandwich. [orders/checkout.ts:61-69] [orders/orders.ts:45-51]

I have no idempotency guard, no lookup by `orderId`, and no reconciliation before recording another success. The ledger happily stores every successful attempt, so once orders retries against a slow network, I will charge again like a damn machine with no brakes. [payments/ledger.ts:11-18] [payments/processor.ts:38-49]

verdict.rootCause: The gateway timeout is shorter than the payment service's normal processing time, so checkout often sees a timeout on a charge that may still succeed upstream. Orders retries that timeout without an idempotency key, and payments records each attempt as a brand-new charge, so the same order can be charged twice.
verdict.judgeLine: The court finds the timeout, the retry, and the missing idempotency all guilty as hell.
